{"effort": "high", "extra": {}, "max_tokens": 8000, "messages": [["user", "## Domain

```json
{
  "id": "dom_158",
  "name": "Average claim turnaround time",
  "topic": "Health Insurance Claims Processing",
  "complexity_tier": "simple",
  "typical_entities_hint": [
    "claim",
    "processing center"
  ],
  "typical_metrics_hint": [
    {
      "name": "mean cycle time",
      "unit": "days"
    },
    {
      "name": "claims closed",
      "unit": "claims/week"
    }
  ],
  "temporal_granularity_hint": "weekly"
}
```

Aim for 200-500 rows and put that number in `emit(n)`.

## What to write

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `scenario_title` | One sentence: the period, the organisations, the analytical focus |
| `data_context` | One paragraph: who collected the data, why, and when |
| `script` | A sequence of the four declaration calls below |
| `intents` | 2-4 analysis intents, each a sentence plus target columns, aggregate and view class |

Write every column name, value, unit, scenario sentence and intent sentence in English.

## The four declaration methods

The script contains only these four calls. No loops, no conditionals, no assignments.

```
dim(name, values, weights=None, parent=None, ordered=None, group=None)
    A category column. `parent` expresses a hierarchy; `weights` is either one
    vector or a distribution per parent value; `ordered` is None, "ordinal" (values
    have a natural order) or "stage" (steps something passes through in sequence);
    `group` names the hierarchy chain, and columns on one chain share a group.
time(name, start, end, freq)
    A time column, freq is daily, weekly or monthly. The calendar fields
    day_of_week, month, quarter and is_weekend are derived automatically -- do not
    declare them yourself.
measure(name, expr, unit, additive)
    A numeric column. additive: counts, amounts and durations add up; ratios,
    percentages, temperatures and scores do not.
emit(n)
    Produce n rows.
```

## Expressions

| Part | How to write it |
|---|---|
| Distribution | `gaussian(mu, sigma)` `lognormal(mu, sigma)` `gamma(shape, scale)` `beta(a, b)` `uniform(low, high)` `poisson(lam)` `exponential(scale)` `mixture(p, a, b)` |
| Category effect | `[column=value]` is a 0/1 indicator; `{"value": number}[column]` is a lookup, and values containing spaces must be quoted |
| Another column | Write its name. A time column evaluates to days since its start |
| Arithmetic | `+ - * / **`, `clip(x, lo, hi)`, `where(condition, a, b)`, `sin` `cos` `log` `exp` `sqrt` |

Dependencies are read out of the expressions, so do not declare them. Statistical
patterns are part of an expression too: an outlier is a multiplicative conditional
term, a trend break is a piecewise term over time, seasonality is a sine over time.

## Constraints

1. One row is one indivisible event; do not lay out a cross product of categories
2. At least 2 dimension groups and at least 2 numeric columns
3. Dependencies must not form a cycle
4. Every symbol in an expression has an explicit numeric definition
5. Declare each numeric column once; do not patch it with later calls
6. Every numeric column declares a unit and additivity
7. Numbers, entities and time windows stay in plausible real-world ranges
8. Size the table to the columns: pick any two category columns you expect to be
   charted together and make sure `n` gives their cross product at least
   5 rows per cell

## View classes for intents

Each intent says which kind of question it answers. There are six:

- `comparison`: which is highest, which is lowest, how they rank
- `trend`: how something moves over time, where it turns
- `composition`: what share each part holds, how the mix shifts
- `relation`: whether two metrics move together
- `distribution`: how spread out values are, whether there are outliers
- `process`: where the largest drop happens along a sequence of stages

`aggregate` is one of SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN, MEDIAN, COUNT, NONE. Summing a
non-additive measure is never legal. Use NONE for a relation between two numeric
columns.

## Worked example

Input:

```json
{
  "name": "Emergency department operations",
  "topic": "Healthcare",
  "complexity_tier": "medium",
  "typical_entities_hint": [
    "hospital",
    "department",
    "triage level"
  ],
  "typical_metrics_hint": [
    {
      "name": "wait_time",
      "unit": "minutes"
    }
  ],
  "temporal_granularity_hint": "daily"
}
```

Output:

```json
{
  "scenario_title": "Emergency department visits and wait times at three metro hospitals, Jan-Jun 2024",
  "data_context": "The county health department compiled per-visit records from three hospitals for January through June 2024 to assess a new triage diversion policy.",
  "script": "dim(\"hospital\", [\"Mercy General\", \"St. Luke's\", \"Riverside\"],\n    weights=[0.40, 0.35, 0.25], group=\"entity\")\ndim(\"department\", [\"Internal Medicine\", \"Surgery\", \"Pediatrics\", \"Trauma\"], parent=\"hospital\",\n    weights={\"Mercy General\": [0.35, 0.25, 0.15, 0.25],\n             \"St. Luke's\": [0.40, 0.20, 0.20, 0.20],\n             \"Riverside\": [0.30, 0.30, 0.15, 0.25]})\ndim(\"severity\", [\"Minor\", \"Moderate\", \"Severe\"], weights=[0.50, 0.35, 0.15],\n    ordered=\"ordinal\", group=\"triage\")\n\ntime(\"visit_date\", start=\"2024-01-01\", end=\"2024-06-30\", freq=\"daily\")\n\nmeasure(\"wait_minutes\",\n        \"lognormal(mu = 2.8 + 0.4*[severity=Moderate] + 0.9*[severity=Severe]\"\n        \"             + 0.2*[hospital=Mercy General],\"\n        \"          sigma = 0.35)\",\n        unit=\"minutes\", additive=True)\nmeasure(\"cost\",\n        \"wait_minutes * 12 + {Minor: 80, Moderate: 260, Severe: 700}[severity] + gaussian(0, 30)\",\n        unit=\"USD\", additive=True)\nmeasure(\"satisfaction\",\n        \"clip(5.2 - wait_minutes / 32 + gaussian(0, 0.3), 1, 5)\",\n        unit=\"points\", additive=False)\n\nemit(900)\n",

    {
      "sentence": "Which hospital and department waits longest",

      "sentence": "Do longer waits go with lower satisfaction",

      ],

  ]
}
```

{"scenario_title":"Weekly claim closures and turnaround times across six regional health-insurance processing centers, January 2023 through June 2024","data_context":"The claims operations analytics team of a mid-sized regional health insurer assembled one record for every claim closed between the first week of January 2023 and the last week of June 2024, drawn from the adjudication platform's closure log and joined to the workflow audit trail. The extract was produced in July 2024 to support a service-level review: leadership wanted to know whether the staged rollout of auto-adjudication rules had actually shortened average cycle time, which processing centers were lagging, and how much of the delay was attributable to outstanding information requests and rework. Each row carries the closing center, the claim type, how the claim arrived, the workflow path it finally took, and the measured duration and effort of that claim.","script":"dim("region", ["Midwest", "South", "West"], weights=[0.38, 0.34, 0.28], group="network")
dim("processing_center",
    ["Des Moines Hub", "Columbus Center", "Atlanta Hub", "Tulsa Overflow Unit", "Phoenix Center", "Portland Center"],
    parent="region",
    weights={"Midwest": [0.55, 0.45, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
             "South": [0.0, 0.0, 0.72, 0.28, 0.0, 0.0],
             "West": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.58, 0.42]},
    group="network")

dim("claim_type", ["Professional", "Outpatient", "Inpatient", "Dental", "Specialty pharmacy"],
    weights=[0.40, 0.24, 0.12, 0.13, 0.11], group="claim")
dim("submission_channel", ["EDI clearinghouse", "Provider portal", "Paper mail"],
    weights=[0.62, 0.26, 0.12], group="intake")
dim("review_path", ["Auto-adjudicated", "Manual review", "Appealed"],
    weights=[0.58, 0.33, 0.09], ordered="stage", group="workflow")

time("closed_week", start="2023-01-02", end="2024-06-24", freq="weekly")

measure("cycle_time_days",
        "lognormal(mu = 1.05 + 0.35*[claim_type=Inpatient] + 0.20*[claim_type=Specialty pharmacy]"
        "             + 0.10*[claim_type=Outpatient] - 0.12*[claim_type=Dental]"
        "             + 0.45*[review_path=Manual review] + 0.85*[review_path=Appealed]"
        "             + 0.28*[submission_channel=Paper mail] + 0.06*[submission_channel=Provider portal]"
        "             - 0.0035*(closed_week/7) + 0.09*sin(closed_week/58.1),"
        "          sigma = 0.40) * (1 + 1.20*[processing_center=Tulsa Overflow Unit])",
        unit="days", additive=True)
measure("information_request_days",
        "clip(cycle_time_days * beta(2, 6), 0, 45)",
        unit="days", additive=True)
measure("rework_touches",
        "poisson(0.35 + 0.55*[review_path=Manual review] + 1.60*[review_path=Appealed]"
        "        + 0.30*[submission_channel=Paper mail])",
        unit="touches", additive=True)
measure("clean_claim_score",
        "clip(0.95 - 0.018*cycle_time_days - 0.06*rework_touches + gaussian(0, 0.04), 0, 1)",
        unit="ratio", additive=False)

emit(420)
